first_impression: It's a cute, very basic herding simulator with a nice low-poly aesthetic and clear UI. But it looks painfully slow, and without any real progression or variety, I'd probably put it down after one or two rounds.
best_things: The lighting changes as the sun sets are actually really pretty and set a great mood.
The UI dashed circle showing exactly where my dog's influence radius is makes the mechanics super readable.
The minimap is clean, useful, and makes navigating the relatively large map easy.

worst_problems.problem: Walking across the map takes forever and is incredibly boring. I spent a minute and a half just holding 'W' with nothing happening.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give me a fast travel to known areas or make the dog way faster when not actively herding.

worst_problems.problem: There's no point to playing more than once. The end screen just says 'Play again' instead of moving to a new level.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add a map with different levels, or let me unlock upgrades or hats for my dog with the stars I earn.

worst_problems.problem: The dog looks like it's sliding on butter because the run animation doesn't match the movement speed at all.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fix the animation blending and speed so it actually looks like the dog's feet are hitting the ground.

worst_problems.problem: The wolf alert UI is this massive, ugly box that pops up and covers a chunk of the screen.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make it a smaller, sleeker notification, or just rely on the in-world red arrows which already do a good job.

worst_problems.problem: The sheep behave like a single gelatinous blob instead of individual animals when grouped up.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add some slight randomized offsets to their movement so they bump into each other and look like a real flock.

boredom_points: The massive trek from the sheepfold at 00:45 all the way to the top left of the map at 02:24 is just holding a direction for almost two minutes with zero gameplay happening.
confusions: What does the 'need 9' mean in the top left? Do I fail the day if I don't get 9? It wasn't entirely obvious until the end screen.
wish_list: A campaign map with different farms to progress through.
More complex terrain puzzles, like gates I have to open or bridges I have to fix.
Different breeds of dogs with unique stats (like a faster sprint or a bigger bark radius).
one_line_review: A relaxing but ultimately shallow herding game that runs out of tricks after the first day.
